translations.reason: The knowledge operator requires epistemic logic, which is not supported in the available formalism
The conclusion depends on the epistemic principle 'if S knows P, then P is true,' which cannot be expressed in classical propositional/first-order logic without modal operators

interpretation_notes: The argument relies on the epistemic entailment Kp → p (if an agent knows p, then p is true), which cannot be formalized in classical logic without modal operators. Both premises and conclusion require modal semantics for accurate representation.
